headline: Post Describing Sleep as 'Just Free Death Trial' Causes Widespread Insomnia
subheadline: Mental health hotlines report spike in calls; post author apologizes
summary: A viral shower thought about the nature of sleep has reportedly made it impossible for thousands to fall asleep.
content:
A Threadit post describing sleep as "just a free death trial—you lie down, stop existing, then wake up and decide if you want to continue" has reportedly caused mass insomnia as readers find themselves unable to stop thinking about it.

"I read it three weeks ago," wrote one user in a follow-up thread. "I haven't slept well since. Every time I close my eyes, I think 'this is a trial run for not existing' and then I'm wide awake contemplating mortality. Thanks for nothing."

The original post, by u/ExistentialExhausted, was intended as a humorous observation. It has since been viewed over 2 million times and directly blamed for an estimated 847,000 hours of lost sleep worldwide.

"I didn't mean to break everyone's ability to rest," u/ExistentialExhausted wrote in an apology post. "I was just tired and thought 'haha what if sleep is practice death' and apparently that thought is contagious and permanent. My bad."

Mental health professionals have noted a spike in sleep-related anxiety calls since the post went viral. "People are calling to ask if sleep is death," reported one hotline volunteer. "We have to explain that no, sleep and death are different. But then they ask 'are they though?' and honestly, at 3 AM, I'm not equipped for that philosophy."

The post has been compared to other "brain-breaking" observations that, once read, cannot be unthought. Previous examples include "your tongue rests somewhere in your mouth" and "you've never seen your own face, only reflections and photos."

Threadit moderators have considered adding a "cognitohazard" warning label to posts that may permanently alter perception, though implementation remains unclear.

At press time, u/ExistentialExhausted reported they also couldn't sleep anymore. "I thought it. Now I can't unthink it. I've destroyed myself too."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
